text:
ashley: Quick heads-up — ran a focused microbatch sweep on the 8xA100 TPxPP (2TP x 4PP) job and hit a stubborn throughput cliff. profiler shows long all-reduce stalls in the middle of the 1F1B window. attaching short summary below. anyone seen this pattern?

mihir: paste the profiler snippet + config?

ashley: here — timeline top lines (aggregated over 200 steps):
```
step,compute_us,allreduce_us,other_us
0-3,1200,450,80
4-7,1180,1700,100  # spike at step 4..7 (bubble region)
8-11,1220,430,90
```
and a flame excerpt: allreduce_wait dominated ~38% of wall time during those mid steps.

carmen: that spike smells like serialized NCCL progress + small microbatch size. what microbatch and global batch did you run?

ashley: microbatch=4, global_batch=32, sequence_len=2048, kv_cache_enabled=true. kernels pinned to fused_matmul_int8 from the kernel selector in the last release PR.

sam: curious — did kernel_selector flip to int8 slow path? sometimes int8 kernel has higher latency per step when comms are frequent. any kernel fallbacks logged?

ashley: logs show selector picked matmul_fused_int8 for most layers. no explicit fallback, but there are warnings around "small_tail_kernels":
```
[kernel_selector] chosen=matmul_fused_int8, latency_est=1.1ms, fallback=no
[runtime] small_tail_kernels detected at pp stage 2, enabling slow_sync_allreduce
```

jen: small_tail_kernels + 1F1B schedule = risk. if the microbatch count doesn't fill the pipeline evenly, you can end up with many tiny all-reduces queued.

ashley: experimented with microbatch=8 earlier — overlap improved but KV cache hit-rate dropped from 98% -> 89% (more cache misses when we changed packing). misses seem to amplify communication.

carmen: that suggests batching heuristics are doing different prefix grouping when microbatch changes. do we change tokenization/packing in the batching layer?

ashley: yes, the batcher merges sequences aggressively for microbatch>=8; that changed kv key distribution. profiler shows more KV-load latency concurrent with all-reduce spikes.

mihir: two separate but interacting issues: (1) kernel selection leads to slower per-tensor compute tail behavior; (2) batching/kv changes increase memory traffic and reduce overlap. we should isolate.

sam: quick experiments to try:
- force float32 matmul kernel for a run (disable fused_int8)
- keep microbatch=4 but tweak packer to preserve kv groupings (no aggressive merge)
- enable NCCL_ASYNC_ALLREDUCE or use our async_allreduce shim (if available)

ashley: ran float32-forced run: allreduce fraction dropped 38% -> 28%, end-to-end throughput +10%. KV hit stayed ~98%. so kernel choice is a big contributor.

jen: interesting. that implies fused_int8 path increases compute tail (maybe due to smaller GEMM blocking) which reduces comm/compute overlap. can you capture per-layer matmul latencies around the PP boundaries?

ashley: attached per-layer (excerpt):
```
layer,pp_stage,matmul_us
12,1,980
13,1,1150  # big tail on layer 13
14,2,1020
15,2,1100
```
layers at PP stage boundary have higher variance on int8.

carmen: can we update kernel selector to prefer kernels with lower tail variance when pipeline-scheduled? maybe weight kernel score by 95th percentile latency rather than mean.

mihir: agree. also add a schedule-aware batching heuristic: keep kv-grouping stable across microbatch sweeps to avoid sudden cache miss patterns.

sam: another immediate mitigation — increase 1F1B fill parameter (fill=2 -> fill=4) so pipeline has fewer empty slots; that reduces frequency of tiny all-reduces. cost is higher memory usage.

ashley: tried fill=4, microbatch=4 => allreduce spikes reduced, but memory climbed ~6GB and we hit OOM on edge configs. tradeoff.

jen: ops:
- mihir: create kernel-selector PR to include tail-variance signal + weight for pipeline schedules
- carmen: add an option in batcher to preserve kv grouping across microbatch changes and add unit test
- ashley: bisect kernel commits between 2345..2360 to find regression (looks like 2352 changed blocking)
- sam: run async_allreduce shim test across 4 configs (mb=4/8, fill=2/4) and post traces

infra-bot: new task created: INF-7621 "bisect fused_int8 perf regression" assigned to ashley, due 3d.

ashley: I'll also attach full perf traces to the ticket. thanks for quick feedback. will follow-up with a short compare report once bisect narrows commit. :thumbsup:

mihir: nice triage. if the kernel fix is non-trivial, we can land batching guardrails first to reduce regression impact.

carmen: FYI I saw similar pattern in a different model (seq_len=1024) last month — I'll dig up that trace and drop it into INF-7621 for reference.

sam: if anyone wants to re-run the float32 control I pushed a short script to infra: `scripts/perf/run_pp_sweep.sh --force-fp32`

ashley: adding that to the ticket now. I'll update here when bisect finds culprit.

jen: great. next sync: brief on Mon standup?

ashley: yep, will have initial bisect result by then.
